verdict_reason: Both kernels match their released references. Block Influence: ran sramshetty/ShortGPT short_gpt/metrics.py::block_influence head-to-head on all 12 real gpt2 block transitions -- worst relative error 2.041e-06 -- and the analytic anchors are exact (identity layer BI = 0.000000000000, sign-flip BI = 2.000000000000). Contribution: RobertCsordas/llm_effective_depth analysis/analyze_norms.py:101 is layer_diff.norm(dim=-1) / inputs.norm(dim=-1).clamp(min=1e-6) accumulated per token and divided by the count, i.e. the mean of per-token ratios with a 1e-6 clamp -- exactly what effective_depth.py:98-110 computes; against a float64 recomputation on real gpt2 the worst relative error is 1.187e-07. Both are stable across the whole scale ladder 1e-30..6.656e17 (mean_BI varies by 2.2e-7, effective_depth_90 constant).
comparable_reason: effective_depth_90 is arithmetically pinned, not measured. Across 4 models it takes only two values: distilgpt2 0.833333 = exactly (L-1)/L with L=6, gpt2 0.916667 = exactly (L-1)/L with L=12, and BOTH pythias exactly 1.000000. The cause is measured: the embedding -> block-0 transition alone holds 72.5% / 70.2% / 30.4% / 52.6% of the total contribution mass (contribution 9.686 / 11.124 / 12.730 / 16.072 against ~0.4 for every later block), so the 90% cumulative quantile always lands on the last or second-to-last layer regardless of how depth is actually used. mean_block_influence is separately a 1/L proxy: 0.29663 (L=6) vs 0.15877 (L=12) for the GPT family and 0.44771 (L=6) vs 0.25643 (L=12) for pythia -- it halves as depth doubles, within family.
github_reason: Downloaded and EXECUTED ShortGPT's block_influence against BLME's _block_influence on 12 real gpt2 transitions: worst relative error 2.041e-06 (float32 noise; BLME's max-relative unit vectors are the more accurate of the two). Downloaded Csordas' analyze_norms.py and read line 101 to confirm the per-token-ratio aggregation and the 1e-6 clamp BLME copies; the reference is a nnsight tracing script that cannot be run standalone here, so the contribution side was verified structurally plus against a float64 recomputation.
paper_reason: ShortGPT publishes BI as a bar chart per layer for Llama-2-7B/13B and Baichuan; no numeric table for a model this host can run. Csordas et al. publish relative-contribution curves, not tabulated values. The papers' qualitative claims ARE reproduced: BI is low in the middle and high at the ends (gpt2 layer 0 = 0.827, layer 3 = 0.027, layer 11 = 0.715), and the second half of layers contributes far less than the first (gpt2 contribution 11.12 at the first transition against 0.40-0.57 mid-stack).
confounds_reason: effective_depth_90 equals (L-1)/L exactly for 2 of 4 models and saturates at 1.0 for the other 2 -- it carries essentially no information beyond n_layers and model family. mean_block_influence scales as ~1/L within family (0.29663 -> 0.15877 for GPT L=6 -> 12; 0.44771 -> 0.25643 for pythia L=6 -> 12). frac_low_influence uses an absolute 0.05 threshold on a quantity that shrinks with L, so it is also depth-driven: 0.1667 / 0.6667 / 0.0000 / 0.0000 on the same 4 models.
defects: COMPARABILITY, THE HEADLINE FINDING: effective_depth_90 is a function of n_layers, not of depth utilization -- it returns exactly (L-1)/L on distilgpt2 and gpt2 and exactly 1.0 on both pythias, because the first transition holds 30-72% of the cumulative contribution mass. The docstring already concedes it is 'a BLME summary INSPIRED BY Csordas et al.' rather than their statistic; the measurement shows it is not usable as a cross-model predictor.

EXTREME-SCALE, UNREACHABLE, AND THE REFERENCE FAILS IDENTICALLY: effective_depth.py:102 forms (_b - _a) in float32 before dividing by the row max, so a block that nearly SIGN-FLIPS a coordinate above ~1.7e38 overflows and the token is silently dropped by the isfinite filter at :108-110. The hand-built fixture h0=[[1,0],[s,0]], h1=[[1.5,0],[-s,0]] at s=2.406e38 reproduces it: contribution 0.5 instead of 1.25. But a UNIFORM rescale of real gpt2 states stays exactly correct all the way to 3.4028e38 (the whole float32 range, 1.11e35x gpt2's actual 3054.12) -- the failure needs a near-antipodal pair at the very top of the range. Csordas' released line 101 does the same subtraction in float32 (.cpu().float()) and overflows identically.

EXTREME-SCALE, UNREACHABLE: .norm() squares, so a relative update above ~6.04e15x the input row overflows the numerator. gpt2's largest per-token relative update, measured over all 12 transitions, is 13.2869 -- a 4.5e14x margin.

PROTOCOL (not implementation): frac_low_influence uses an absolute BI threshold of 0.05 on a quantity that shrinks with depth, so it is not a like-for-like fraction across models; the docstring correctly says ShortGPT defines no threshold.
